newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pioneer Int'l seen posting profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Int'l seen posting profit fall.

text.p: Building materials supplier and petroleum group Pioneer International Ltd is expected to report its first profit fall in four years on Wednesday when it reports results for the year to June 30.
In Australia, weaker results are expected for both the core building materials division and the 50 percent held petrol refiner and retailer Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (APPL).
Analysts estimates for Pioneer's pre-abnormal net profit range between A$210 million and A$220 million with a median of about A$214 million, down from A$252.2 million a year ago.
However analysts said Pioneer was likely to pay a final dividend at nine cents a share, level with the 1995/96 final dividend and making 18 cents for the 1996/97 year.
The maintenance of the dividended reflected a better outlook for 1997/98, they said.
J.B. Were & Son building materials analyst John North estimated a profit of between A$210 million and A$220 million.
"Out of the four building materials markets we expect Australia and Europe to be down, the U.S. and Asia to be up, and refiner dividends significantly down on last year," North said.
Pioneer has operations in about 16 countries.
On balance, the overseas operations are likely to report a higher profit in 1996/97, analysts said.
ANZ Securities building materials analyst Sean Cooney forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$212 million for 1996/97.

Chris Haynes, building materials analyst at BT Securities forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$213 million while a Melbourne-based analyst forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$213.7 million for the year to June.
Analysts said the Australian building materials market was expected to pick up in 1997/98 along with stronger domestic economic growth and an improvement in refiner margins at APPL.
"You would expected the U.S. to be better (in 1997/98), you would hope Europe starts to turn around, but Asia is the big question mark this year," the Melbourne analyst said.
Pioneer was expected to report a pre-abnormals net profit of about A$270 million in 1997/98.
Analysts said they did not expect Pioneer to make any announcement on plans for its stake in APPL on Wednesday.
In February, Pioneer appointed investment banks J.P. Morgan and Macquarie Bank to help review its APPL asset.
APPL is jointly owned with Caltex Australia Ltd, which has first option over Pioneer's stake if it sells out.
"There is no need for them to be in a fire sale. They don't need the money because there are few opportunities for them to buy anything with that money," one Sydney-based analyst said.
Pioneer has low debt and has the capability to fund an acquisition of over A$1 billion.
Shares in the Sydney-based group closed two cents up at A$4.82 on Friday.
The shares have risen 30 percent from A$3.70 since the end of June 1996 while the broader market has risen 19 percent.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1813
